bibliographic.title: Generative AI in healthcare: an implementation science informed translational path on application, integration and governance
bibliographic.citation_apa: Reddy, S. (2024). Generative AI in healthcare: An implementation science informed translational path on application, integration and governance. Implementation Science, 19, 27. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13012-024-01357-9

methodology.method_family: implementation science debate; technology acceptance model (TAM); NASSS model
methodology.study_design: DEBATE article providing conceptual overview and translational pathway
methodology.technology_context: generative AI capable of generating text and images applied to clinical medicine, billing, diagnosis, treatment and research

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article explicitly addresses generative AI application, integration and governance in healthcare using implementation science frameworks, with attention to privacy, security, risk mitigation and ethical/medico-legal concerns. The provided text does not substantiate a primary focus on conversational systems, LLMs, or operational conversational governance mechanisms, so it is better classified as supporting rather than central evidence for the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and abstract excerpts were supplied; Python triage reported conversational-term hits not visible in the provided text, so full-text verification is needed.

appraisal.notes: DEBATE article offering framework-informed argument rather than empirical study; aims and governance considerations are clearly stated, but no primary data, sampling or systematic review method is described in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is coherent and relevant to generative AI governance and integration in regulated healthcare, but the supplied text is conceptual, non-empirical, and does not demonstrate conversational or LLM-specific governance depth.

coding.theme: Implementation-science-informed governance and integration of generative AI in healthcare
coding.subtheme: Translational adoption pathway with risk and ethical safeguards
rq_alignment: generative AI governance in regulated settings
risk mitigation and compliance considerations in healthcare AI adoption

synthesis.main_claim: Generative AI can improve healthcare if introduced through implementation-science-informed, incremental adoption with explicit governance, risk mitigation, privacy/security safeguards and preserved clinician expertise.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes a translational path for healthcare generative AI using TAM and NASSS to anticipate adoption barriers, engage stakeholders and support responsible integration.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text is a conceptual DEBATE piece without empirical evaluation; conversational AI, LLM-specific controls, audit/logging, human oversight/contestation and post-deployment monitoring are not evidenced in the excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on governance and implementation considerations for generative AI in regulated healthcare; consult full text before treating as central evidence for conversational LLM governance.
